title: Recapture, adoption and unit-safe calculation
objective: Explain why 'users × minutes × hourly rate' is incomplete.
clearance: Rewritten draft; pending SME and partner clearance

blocks.x: A capacity model is a chain of explicit assumptions. Every link needs a unit and an evidence label, and none should be quietly assumed to be 100%.
A defensible capacity model accounts for:

items: **Adoption:** the share who actively use the capability.
**Frequency:** events per active user per workday.
**Time:** minutes per event, converted once to hours.
**Removable share and coverage:** how much of the burden Glean can realistically remove, and for what share of events.
**Recapture:** the share of freed capacity that becomes useful business output.
**Loaded rate:** the value of an hour, labeled as capacity value, not cash.

blocks.x: Glean's Value Playbook calls the productivity recapture rate the most consequential assumption in any value model. It answers this question: of the time Glean saves, how much actually converts into measurable business output? The honest answer is not all of it. Recapture is not the share of users who log in; that is adoption. Ask the business owner for a reallocation plan, meaning what the team will do with the time, before choosing a recapture assumption.
If the time-saved input is already measured, for example as minutes saved per event, don't apply a removable-share discount to it again. Check what each input means before applying a factor.

blocks.label: Boundary
blocks.x: This module's ROI Lab uses fictional values. Glean's internal calculator defaults are not customer facts. Don't present them as the customer's numbers without validation.
Each factor narrows the estimate. Apply each one once, in a visible formula.

practice.x: A colleague's model is "users × minutes saved × hourly rate." Explain why it is incomplete.

worked.x: It leaves out adoption, event frequency, and the time period. It doesn't convert minutes to hours explicitly. It ignores how much of the work is really removable, and assumes 100% recapture with no uncertainty adjustment.
Document each input with its evidence label, convert units once, and make sure discounts don't overlap.
